title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The page closes the summary scholie of p.56 and starts a new construction.

**(i) End of the scholie.** Grothendieck reviews the successive names of the structure he has been studying: first F ("but we thought about it less!"), then A or (A,F), then L, and finally Σ, a "spatios". He notes that spatios are especially convenient for stating the axioms of the '∘-W…ts' (reading uncertain; possibly '∘-events' or '∘-ateliers'), better than the usual spatial ateliers. From the previous page, an atelier amounts to a spatios (Σ, ≤, c) with a family A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ) satisfying axioms Abspat 1, 2.

**(ii) Spatios attached to a set with a relation.** Fix a set E with a symmetric relation |∘| (read: x and y are 'disjoint' or 'orthogonal'). The relation is first called anti-reflexive, then weakened to allow reflexive points subject to one condition: x|∘|x ⇒ ∀y∈E, x|∘|y. So a self-disjoint point must be disjoint from everything, like an empty or zero element.

The marginal NB says the category of such objects is equivalent to the strictly anti-reflexive case. The degenerate 'zero' points add nothing essential. The next page confirms the objects are equivalently (strict) graphs, and names them 'dispositions'.

**(iii) Morphisms.** For E = (E, |∘|_E) and E' = (E', |∘|_{E'}), a correspondence φ: E → 𝔓(E') is a morphism if, for all x, y ∈ E and all x' ∈ φ(x), y' ∈ φ(y): x|∘|y ⇒ x'|∘|y'. Morphisms compose as correspondences: (ψ∘φ)(x) = ∪_{x'∈φ(x)} ψ(x'). The identity is x ↦ {x}. This is a subcategory of the Kleisli category of the power-set monad, i.e. sets and relations, consisting of relations that preserve orthogonality. A marginal example concerns the identity correspondence (rest illegible).

**(iv) Where this goes (next page).** A morphism α induces ᾱ: 𝔓(E) → 𝔓(E'), A ↦ ∪_{x∈A} α(x). Composing with inclusion and a 'support/closure' map gives α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'}, with α_*(S) = suppr°(ᾱ(S)). So Σ_E is presumably a lattice of 'closed' subsets of E (most plausibly the subsets closed under the biorthogonal/disjointness Galois connection), carrying ≤ and a complement c. This would make (E, |∘|) ↦ Σ_E a functor from dispositions to spatios, giving a large supply of examples of spatios.
errors: Internal inconsistency, corrected on the page itself: the relation is first called 'anti-réflexive', then allowed reflexive points under the condition x|∘|x ⇒ ∀y, x|∘|y. The NB says this generalization is inessential (equivalent category).

The morphism condition allows φ(x) = ∅, and does not require reflection of orthogonality or any 'covering' property. This is fine as a definition, but the induced α_* on closed sets need not preserve complements; that is presumably why the next page restricts its domain ('définie sur les …').

ideas.what: Sets with a symmetric (anti-reflexive) 'disjointness' relation as basic objects generating 'spatios' Σ_E; equivalent to simple graphs; called 'dispositions' on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces (Dacey spaces) / simple graphs; lattice of orthoclosed subsets
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. C. Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall (1970s) in quantum logic; orthoclosure via Birkhoff polarity

ideas.what: Allowing degenerate self-disjoint points (x|∘|x ⇒ x orthogonal to all), with the remark that the category is equivalent to the strict case.
Morphisms as orthogonality-preserving correspondences E → 𝔓(E'), composed as correspondences (Kleisli composition for the power-set monad).
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality-preserving relations / Kleisli morphisms of the power-set monad; cf. morphisms of orthogonality spaces and Chu-space style maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (e.g. Moore, Vetterlein in orthogonality-space literature; Kleisli 1965 for the categorical form)

ideas.what: Spatios Σ as the preferred language for axiomatizing 'ateliers' (abstract spaces of figures), replacing earlier formulations F, (A,F), L.
ideas.modern_name: Lattice-theoretic/pointless axiomatization of spaces of figures (closest: complete ortholattices / locale-like structures)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's construction of spatios Σ_E from a set with a symmetric 'disjointness' relation, functorial in orthogonality-preserving correspondences, appears to rediscover orthogonality spaces and their lattices of orthoclosed sets (complete ortholattices) from quantum logic. He does this independently, in the context of his 1986 'ateliers' theory of abstract spaces of figures. Neither literature cites the other.
missed.quote: aux ens. E munis d'une relation symétrique anti-réflexive (notée |∘|_X) … x|∘|x ⟹ ∀y∈E, x|∘|y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If Σ_E is indeed the orthoclosure lattice, his 'ateliers/spatios' framework links to a well-developed theory (orthogonality spaces, Dacey/Foulis–Randall test spaces, recent categorical work by Vetterlein and others). His morphism notion via correspondences may offer a functorial setting that differs from those usually used there. This remains speculative until Σ_E's definition on earlier pages is checked.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a clean but elementary category (graphs/'dispositions' with correspondence morphisms) feeding into Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 'spatios/ateliers' theory. The mathematics itself is routine. The mild interest lies in the apparent independent rediscovery of orthogonality spaces and their ortholattices inside an unpublished program on abstract spatial structures.
transcription_corrections: 'Soride des spatios' should read 'Soient des spatios' or 'Sorte des spatios' (the underlined word is likely 'Soride'/'Sorite', i.e. 'Sorite des spatios Σ_E associés aux ens. E munis d'une relation…').
'd'une relation symétrique anti{+ré+}flexive': the inserted word above is 'stricte'? Unclear; the main text clearly reads 'symétriques antiréflexives (notée |∘|_X)'.
The marginal NB plausibly reads: 'NB La catégorie des ∘-options est équivalente à celle des [objets où] x|∘|x ⟹ ∀y≠x …', i.e. an equivalence with the strictly anti-reflexive case.
'Soient E=(E,|∘|_E), E'=(E',|∘|_{E'}) munis de relations symétriques': the leading '1°)' may be '2°)' or a struck symbol.
In 'une correspondance E —φ→ 𝔓(E') (compatible …)' the parenthetical likely reads '(i.e. compatible à |∘|_E, |∘|_{E'})', attached to the following 'est dite un morphisme de E dans E' si'.
The marginal 'Ex.' likely reads 'Ex. La corr. identique E → E est un morphisme' (partially illegible).
